record.original_question: Denote by p(w) the smallest period of a word w ∈ Σ+ . Let X ⊆ Σ+ satisfying p(x) < p(w) for all x ∈ X. Is it true that w has at most |X| + 1 − r(X) disjoint X-factorizations?

evidence.quote: Denote by p(w) the smallest period of a word w ∈ Σ+ . Let X ⊆ Σ+ satisfying p(x) < p(w) for all x ∈ X. Is it true that w has at most |X| + 1 − r(X) disjoint X-factorizations?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Sigma$ be a finite alphabet and $\Sigma^+$ the set of nonempty finite words over $\Sigma$. For a word $w \in \Sigma^+$, denote by $p(w)$ the smallest period of $w$, i.e., the least positive integer $p$ such that $w[i] = w[i+p]$ for all valid indices $i$.

For a finite set $X \subseteq \Sigma^+$, the (combinatorial) rank $r(X)$ is defined as the minimum cardinality of a set $Y \subseteq \Sigma^+$ such that $X \subseteq Y^*$, where $Y^*$ denotes the submonoid generated by $Y$.

An $X$-factorization of $w$ is a sequence $(x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_k)$ with each $x_i \in X$ and $w = x_1 x_2 \cdots x_k$. Two $X$-factorizations $(x_1,\ldots,x_k)$ and $(y_1,\ldots,y_\ell)$ of the same word $w$ are called disjoint if the sets of "cut positions" $\{|x_1\cdots x_i| : 1 \le i \le k-1\}$ and $\{|y_1\cdots y_j| : 1 \le j \le \ell-1\}$ are disjoint.

Suppose $X \subseteq \Sigma^+$ is finite and satisfies $p(x) < p(w)$ for every $x \in X$. Prove or disprove: the number of pairwise disjoint $X$-factorizations of $w$ is at most $|X| + 1 - r(X)$.
artifact.status_search_result: Web search did not return any direct evidence of resolution of this specific question on the number of disjoint X-factorizations bounded by |X|+1-r(X) under the period condition p(x) < p(w). Related defect-type results for bi-infinite words and combinatorial rank exist, but no source confirms the conjecture is proved or refuted in the finite-word setting stated here.

status_evidence.title: A defect theorem for bi-infinite words
status_evidence.snippet: If a nonperiodic bi-infinite word w has two X-factorizations, then the combinatorial rank of X is at most card(X)-1.
status_evidence.claim: Related defect/rank results exist for bi-infinite words but do not directly resolve the stated finite-word problem.
